data.name: Jawharah
data.gender_notes: Jawharah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jawharah means 'jewel' in Arabic. It is a unisex name but more commonly used for girls. It is derived from the word 'jawhara' which means 'precious stone' or 'gem'. The name Jawharah carries the meaning “Jewel” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Jawharah usually hope their child will grow to embody jewel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name reflecting purity, rarity, and value.
data.etymology: Jawharah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jewel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jawharah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Jawharah
in_english.meaning: A precious stone, a gem, a treasure
in_english.long_meaning: Jawharah, an Arabic name meaning 'precious jewel' or 'treasure,' is derived from the root word 'jawhar,' signifying 'excellence,' 'beauty,' and 'value.' It reflects the Islamic appreciation for beauty, refinement, and spiritual worth. Jawharah is often associated with qualities like integrity, generosity, and inner radiance. Its usage across diverse Muslim cultures underscores its timeless appeal and enduring significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jawharah holds significant cultural impact as it has been used in various contexts throughout Islamic history. In Arabic poetry, the term 'jawhara' is often used to describe the beauty and preciousness of an object or a person. Moreover, Jawharah is also the name of a famous figure in Islamic history, Jawhar al-Sültani, who was the vizier (chief advisor) and the general of the Fatimid Caliph Al-Mustansir billah. Jawhar is best known for his role in bringing the emerald green treasure of the Fatimids from Zabid (Yemen) to Cairo, Egypt in 1009 CE. The treasure was presented to the caliph as a gift, and it is now known as the "Treasury of Jawhar" or the "Casket of Wonders." This treasure is considered to be one of the largest and most valuable treasures ever discovered and contains numerous precious and semi-precious stones, gold, silver, and exotic items such as ivory and porcelain.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jawharah also holds deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the preciousness and worth of every human being in the eyes of Allah. Islamic teachings advocate the inherent value and dignity of every human life. The name Jawharah reminds us that each and every one of us is a precious gem, a 'jewel' in the sight of Allah. It is a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge, practicing good deeds, and striving for self-improvement in order to increase our worth in the eyes of Allah.
